transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I almost feel silly bringing it up, but... I’ve been having a hard time not thinking about this scar on my wrist. I know it’s probably not as noticeable as it seems to me, but when I’m at church or playing bridge, I feel like people’s eyes go right to it, like it’s the first thing they see about me now. I’m not sure if that’s the sort of thing you help with, but it’s been bothering me.
Has this concern about your scar been affecting your daily life or relationships in any way?

A little, yes… I mean, I’m still managing, mostly. But I have been late turning in some of my bookkeeping work because I get sort of caught up trying to make sure my wrist is covered or not noticeable before I go in or send things off.

And I’ve skipped a few choir practices and some theater volunteer things, which I don’t like admitting. It’s just… I start worrying people will notice it, and then it feels easier not to go. That probably sounds a bit silly, doesn’t it?
Do you find yourself repeatedly thinking about the scar, even when you're not in situations where it might be noticed?

Yes… I do, though I try not to make too much of it. It just sort of pops into my mind, even when I’m not doing anything where anyone would see it. I’ll think, “It’s probably not really that bad,” but then I picture being at church or playing bridge and feeling like everyone’s eyes go straight to my wrist, like it’s the first thing they notice about me. I know that may not be entirely reasonable, but it’s hard to shake.
Do you think people would judge you or think less of you if they noticed the scar?

I don’t know if I’d say they’d judge me exactly… maybe that sounds too strong. It’s more that I keep feeling like if they notice it, their eyes will go right to my wrist and that’ll be the first thing they see about me now. 

I do know, at least in my head, that it’s probably not as bad as it looks to me. But at church or bridge, I still worry people are noticing it. Does that make sense?
Is it specifically the appearance of the scar that bothers you, or is it more about what you think it might mean to others about you?

I think… it’s mostly the way it looks, if I’m being honest. I know the scar on my wrist is probably not as bad as it seems to me, and I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is.

But when I’m at church or playing bridge, I keep feeling like everyone’s eyes go right to it, like it’s the first thing they notice about me now. I suppose that’s more about the appearance than anything it “means,” if that makes sense.
Is it only your wrist with the scar that you're concerned about, or are there other parts of your body that you worry about as well?

Mostly just the wrist, yes. I don’t really have other parts of my body I worry about in the same way. I mean, I know the scar is probably not as bad as it looks to me, but when I’m at church or playing bridge, I keep feeling like people’s eyes go right to it… like it’s the first thing they notice now. I hope that makes sense.
Is there something specific about the appearance of the scar that bothers you, such as its size, shape, or color?

I’m not sure it’s one specific thing like the shape or color… maybe just that it’s there and visible on my wrist. I know, logically, it’s probably not as noticeable as it feels to me.

But when I’m at church or playing bridge, I just get this feeling that people’s eyes go right to it, like it’s the first thing they notice about me now. Maybe that sounds a bit silly, but that’s what it feels like.
Do you think your concern about the scar's appearance is greater than how others actually perceive it?

Yes… I suppose it probably is. I mean, I know the scar on my wrist is likely not as bad as it looks to me, and I’m trying not to make too much of it.

But when I’m at church or playing bridge, I just keep feeling like everyone’s eyes go right to it, like it’s the first thing they notice about me now. Maybe they don’t really see it that way, but it feels that way to me.
How much distress would you say this concern about your scar is causing you?

It’s… not unbearable, I wouldn’t want to make it sound dramatic. But it does bother me more than I’d like to admit, I suppose.

I know the scar on my wrist probably isn’t as bad as it looks to me, but when I’m at church or playing bridge, I keep feeling like people’s eyes go right to it, like it’s the first thing they notice now. So yes, it causes me some distress… mostly embarrassment and feeling self-conscious. Does that answer what you mean?
Is there something about your appearance, aside from the scar, that you feel is flawed or defective?

No, I don’t think so… not really. I mean, I’m 64, so of course there are little things I don’t love, but nothing I’d call flawed or defective.

It’s really just the scar that’s been on my mind. I hope that makes sense.
Do you feel like the scar makes you imperfect in some way?

A little, yes… though I feel silly saying it that way. I know the scar on my wrist probably isn’t as bad as it looks to me.

But when I’m at church or playing bridge, I keep feeling like everyone’s eyes go right to it, like it’s the first thing they notice about me now. So I suppose it does make me feel… less put together, maybe imperfect. Is that what you mean?
Do you find it difficult to stop thinking about the scar when it pops into your mind?

Yes… I suppose it can be difficult, though I wouldn’t say it takes over completely.

It’s more that once I notice it, or even think about being at church or bridge, my mind sort of goes back to it. I’ll tell myself, “It’s probably not as noticeable as I think,” but then I still feel like everyone’s eyes are going right to my wrist, like it’s the first thing they see. So yes, it can be hard to shake off sometimes. Is that the sort of thing you mean?
Has your concern about the scar been interfering with your ability to concentrate on other things you need to do?

A bit, yes… I hate to admit that, because I don’t want it to sound like I’m making excuses.

With my bookkeeping work, I’ve been late turning things in a couple of times because I get distracted fussing over my wrist or thinking about whether someone might notice it. And I’ve skipped some choir and theater volunteer things too, just because I got so caught up trying to make sure it wouldn’t show.

It’s not constant, but… yes, it has gotten in the way some.
Does thinking about the scar ever feel like it's intruding into your thoughts, even when you're trying to focus on something else?

Yes… sometimes. I don’t want to overstate it, because I know the scar on my wrist probably isn’t as bad as it looks to me.

But it does sort of pop in when I’m trying to pay attention to something else, especially if I’m thinking about church or bridge. I’ll start wondering if people are looking at it, like their eyes go right to my wrist and that’s the first thing they notice about me now. I try to tell myself that’s probably not true, but the thought still comes in anyway. Is that what you mean by intruding?
Do you feel like you're thinking about the scar more often than you want to?

Yes… more than I’d like, I suppose.

I know, realistically, the scar on my wrist is probably not as bad as it looks to me. But when I’m at church or playing bridge, I keep feeling like everyone’s eyes go right to it, like it’s the first thing they notice about me now.

I’m not sure if that sounds silly, but… yes, I do think about it more than I want to.
Do you think that if the scar were gone, you would no longer feel self-conscious about how others perceive you?

I think… maybe I would feel less self-conscious, yes. I don’t want to say it would fix everything about how I feel, because that sounds a little too neat.

But the scar is what I keep coming back to. I know it’s probably not as noticeable as it seems to me, but when I’m at church or playing bridge, I keep feeling like people’s eyes go right to my wrist, like that’s the first thing they see now. So if it weren’t there… I suppose I’d feel more at ease. Does that make sense?
Has your worry about the scar affected your relationships with family or friends?

A little, yes… though I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is.

With family and friends, I suppose it’s more that I’ve pulled back from some things. I’ve skipped a few choir and theater volunteer commitments because I get so caught up trying to make sure my wrist won’t be noticed. And with work, I’ve been late turning in some bookkeeping things for the same reason.

I know that’s not exactly a relationship problem, but it does affect how dependable I am, I guess… which I don’t feel good about. Does that answer what you mean?
Is there something specific about your appearance, related to the scar or otherwise, that you feel is flawed or defective and that you think others might notice?

Yes… mainly the scar on my wrist. I know it’s probably not as bad or as noticeable as it seems to me, and I don’t want to make too much of it.

But when I’m at church, or playing bridge, I feel like people’s eyes go right to it—like it’s the first thing they notice about me now. I suppose that’s the part that feels… flawed, if that’s the word. Does that answer what you mean?
Do you think the scar makes you feel imperfect in a way that you believe others would notice or care about?

Yes… I think that’s fair to say. I don’t mean that everyone is actually staring, and I know the scar on my wrist is probably not as bad as it looks to me.

But when I’m at church or playing bridge, I keep feeling like people’s eyes go right to it, like it’s the first thing they notice about me now. So yes, it does make me feel a bit… imperfect, I guess. I hope that makes sense.
Do you find it difficult to control your thoughts about the scar when they come into your mind?

Yes… sometimes. I try not to let it take over, and I know the scar on my wrist is probably not as bad as it looks to me.

But when the thought comes up—especially if I’m at church or playing bridge—it’s hard to just put it aside. I keep thinking people’s eyes go right to it, like it’s the first thing they notice about me now. I’m not sure if that’s what you mean by difficult to control, but… yes, a bit.
